title: Orchestrate stable retry budgets and circuit-breaker handshakes across regions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Services and client SDKs handle retries, timeouts, and hedged requests inconsistently. During partial region outages or capacity pressure we observe retry storms that exacerbate downstream load, circuit-breaker thrash, and cascading SLO violations. Goal: Define and implement a standardized, SLO-driven retry / timeout / backoff choreography combined with circuit-breaker-aware retry budgets and coordinated hedged request behavior. The implementation should span runtime, gateway, and SDK layers so apps get predictable semantics without ad-hoc per-service tuning.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All platform SDKs implement the new retry-budget header and obey circuit-breaker handshake semantics by default (opt-out in advanced config).
2) Runtime exposes per-tenant and per-route retry budget metrics; dashboards show budget burn rate vs SLO slack and trigger automated shed or fallback when budget exhausted.
3) Multi-region failover respects regional capacity signals: requests are routed to fallback regions only if retry budget and circuit-breaker allow it, preventing cross-region amplification.

4) Hedged requests are limited by a coordinated token scheme (global per-client token bucket) to avoid duplicate hedges causing load spikes; tests show hedging reduces p99 latency without increasing total token consumption beyond budget.
5) Idempotency key guidelines documented and SDK helper included for common operations; server gracefully rejects non-idempotent retries for unsafe endpoints.
6) Integration tests and canary rollout demonstrate reduced cascade rate during induced regional latency spikes compared to baseline.
technical_design: Summary: Introduce a small, composable protocol that all callers and services speak: 1) Retry Budget: a per-client (API key/tenant) token-bucket carried in a header (X-RI-Retry-Budget-Id) and observed via runtime metrics. The router maintains a borrowable ‘regional slack’ pool and returns budget diagnostics on responses (X-RI-Budget-Remaining, X-RI-Budget-Reset). 2) Circuit- Breaker Handshake: before attempting retries beyond 1 attempt, client SDKs issue a lightweight ‘probe’ that checks circuit state via a fast metadata endpoint (internal) or by observing specific response codes/headers. 3) Hedged Request Coordination: SDKs implement a non-deterministic hedging algorithm that consults the retry budget and circuit state; hedges are allowed only if a token is available from the client-side hedging bucket. 4) Server-side Enforcement: runtime enforces max retry attempts per logical request and rejects extra attempts with 429+RetryLimit headers to prevent amplification. 5) Backoff Profile: standardized backoff profiles (conservative, normal, aggressive) map to SLO classes. Profiles encode jitter, max backoff, and total retry budget cost. 6) Idempotency: Use a canonical header (Idempotency-Key). TTL of keys is configurable by route (default 24h). Non-idempotent route attempts with retry >0 produce a Clear-Directive header asking SDK to stop retries and surface as customer-impacting error. 7) Observability: new metrics: retry_budget_remaining, retry_budget_burn_rate, hedged_request_rate, cb_open_percent, shed_rate. Traces must correlate hedged spans with shared idempotency-key to avoid duplicated work attribution.
sdk_contract_changes: Add header support: Idempotency-Key, X-RI-Retry-Budget-Id, X-RI-Budget-Remaining, X-RI-Budget-Reset, X-RI-Retry-Profile
Expose a RetryBudget API in SDKs: checkBudget(), reserveHedgeToken(), releaseBudgetToken()

Default behavior: SDK will perform at most one soft retry (with conservative profile) for idempotent endpoints. Hedging disabled by default for mobile SDKs; enabled for server SDKs behind a feature flag.
Backwards compat: SDKs fallback to legacy behavior when headers are absent; runtime will emit deprecation logs if callers don't adopt protocol within deprecation window.
rollout_plan: Phased rollout over 6 weeks: Week 1-2: Merge SDK support behind feature flag; runtime adds budget metrics and headers but does not enforce limits (observability-only). Week 3-4: Enable server-side soft enforcement in canary region (eu-central-1) for non-critical tenants. Week 5: Expand enforcement to all regions for internal tenants and Recommended customers. Week 6: Enforce by default with opt-out for legacy enterprise customers and provide migration tooling. Must include a coordinated communications plan, deprecation warnings, and customer-facing docs.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: retry budget burn rate, hedged request latency delta, cb_open_percent by region, percent of requests with Idempotency-Key. Alerts: budget burn rate > 80% for 5m AND p99 latency degrade > 20% => Pager. Circuit-breaker thrash (open/close cycles > 10 in 5m) => SEV2. Hedging-induced amplification (hedged_request_rate * mean_tokens > threshold) => runbook: reduce hedging multiplier and rollback feature flag.
test_plan: Unit tests for SDK budget APIs and header propagation. Integration tests: simulated regional latency with the chaos harness validating no amplification when retries happen; hedging test asserts at most one backend non-idempotent call per logical request when Idempotency-Key present. Load test: create a tenant with small retry budget and verify client-side budget prevents downstream saturation. Canary validation: A/B traffic split measuring p50/p95/p99 and total token consumption.
open_questions: 1) TTL for Idempotency-Key per route: default 24h acceptable or should long-running batch jobs get 7d?
2) How granular should retry budgets be: per-API-key, per-service, or per-route? Initial proposal: per-API-key with per-route override.
3) Should the runtime proactively re-fill client budgets during low-load windows (borrowing model)?
4) Interaction with existing rate-limiting layer: priority of enforcement between quota vs retry budget?
5) Legal/compliance for logging idempotency keys: keys may contain PII; do we need hashing at ingestion?
